summary: The note surveys how local governments are responding to climate change through proactive policies, profiling Greenville, Seaport City, Sunnyvale, Riverwood, Horizon Hills, and the Local Climate Advocates Network (LCAN). Each example covers a distinct approach, including adaptation planning, living shorelines, solar adoption, riverfront restoration, climate education, and peer learning. It concludes that grassroots, engaged governance can produce tangible outcomes and that other municipalities can follow these models.
one_line: Profiles of local government climate initiatives in Greenville, Seaport City, Sunnyvale, Riverwood, Horizon Hills and LCAN show grassroots policy driving resilience.
key_facts: On October 5, 2023, Mayor Angela Martinez of Greenville unveiled the Climate Adaptation and Resilience Plan (CARP), developed with local environmental groups and stakeholders.
Greenville's CARP includes enhancing green infrastructure, expanding urban tree canopy to reduce heat islands, and retrofitting buildings to withstand extreme weather.
Greenville has incentivized businesses to adopt green practices and is working toward a circular economy that merges waste reduction with job creation.
Seaport City's council decided in December 2023 to elevate building codes and invest in natural barriers, after which residents noted a decrease in flood-related disruptions.

On January 15, 2024, the Seaport City Turnaround Taskforce launched a collaboration of engineers, community leaders, and ecologists to create living shorelines that also restore oyster habitats and provide recreational spaces.
As of April 9, 2024, Sunnyvale's Solar Surge program has converted more than 35% of the city's rooftops to solar energy.
Councilwoman Renita Singh spearheaded Solar Surge, which offers workshops and funding for low-income households to join the solar transition.

Riverwood's Riverfront Revival project, initiated September 21, 2023, turns a neglected riverine corridor into a space that manages stormwater and provides wildlife habitat, following Mayor Tom Bannister's call to "co-create with nature".
Community workshops led by local ecologists in October 2023 shaped Riverwood's vision of native plantings, bioswales, and boardwalks.

Horizon Hills launched its "Climatic Classroom" initiative on November 12, 2023, led by Superintendent Lydia Ramirez, integrating climate literacy into the K-12 curriculum with school gardens, local weather stations, and field trips.
The Local Climate Advocates Network (LCAN) was launched on February 2, 2024, founded by a coalition of local government leaders including Mayor Howard Chen of Bayside City.
LCAN uses a peer-to-peer learning approach that has catalyzed local policy reforms from sustainable transport initiatives to community-led recycling programs.
